nodes.title: Configurable type for webContents
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

`webContents` gets assigned a `type` on creation. For `BrowserWindow` and `BrowserView` this type is `window` or `browserView`. Webviews always get the type `webview` (this is a hardcoded string: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/lib/browser/guest-view-manager.ts#L102C5-L102C20 )

Because of that `webview` type, `webContents` for webviews are excluded when getting the list of pages through Puppeteer: https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.browser.pages which will only list the `page` type webContents, which it seems both `window` and `browserView` resolve to.

I encountered this issue when trying to set up [chrome-devtools-mcp](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/) to work with [Polypane](https://polypane.app). In Polypane, webviews are conceptually pages but since they are excluded from Puppeteers `browser.pages()` call, they do not show up in the MCP. Having more control over the types of webContents would allow my app to work with this tooling.

### Proposed Solution

It would be nice if there was some way to set the type of a `webview` to (resolve to) `page` rather than `webview`. I'm not too concerned with how, but here are a few options:

- `webContent`s already have a [getType()](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-contents#contentsgettype) method, add a setter.
- Extend the webview tag with a new `type` attribute that can be set to `page` that in turn overwrites the type on the guestView when specified.

These could both either be set as strings, or a number that refers to a pre-specified value (backgroundPage = 0, window = 1 etc). 

An alternative would be a boolean attribute or method to set the type of a webview to `page` when specified or `webview` when not.

### Alternatives Considered

chrome-devtools-mcp can also be updated to show webview types along page types. This means circumventing the `puppeteer.browser.pages()` api and using the CDP JSON endpoint to build up the list of webContents to include both types, and using that instead.

Over in Chrome land, both the `background_page` and `webview` types are not a concern anymore so they might prefer to not make this change.

Another option is to modify Puppeteer to add an argument to browser.pages() to return all webContents, or a different filtering, than just `page`.

### Additional Information

_No response_

Other Linux

Archlinux + KDE + Wayland

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

38.5.0, 39.0.0-alpha.5 (broken in 39.0.0-alpha.6, https://github.com/electron/electron/compare/v39.0.0-alpha.5...v39.0.0-alpha.6)

_The Chromium v142 upgrade caused the regression. v38.x is working correctly._

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When I change the system theme (I'm using latest KDE Plasma v6.5.1 + Wayland), electron should be able to recognize it at runtime. It currently recognizes it correctly on startup, but doesn't work if the system theme is changed during runtime.

### Actual Behavior

When I change the system theme at runtime (electron app running), electron v39 doesn't correctly recognize the theme. shouldUseDarkColors is reported incorrectly (inverse). This causes things like "window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)');" to be reported incorrectly. This is very recent regression as this works perfectly fine when I revert back to using any v38.x.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/lone-cloud/2211e0b707c8c8771eb060d9ad9c403f

### Additional Information

nodes.title: Add possibility to access the context menu programmatically
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

I use Playwright for end-to-end testing an Electron application. Currently, it is not possible to access a context/popup menu in Playwright. I made [an issue there](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/11100) and it is speculated, that something from your side has to be implemented, e.g. `Menu.getContextMenu()` as a counterpart to `Menu.getApplicationMenu()`.

For me, it doesn't matter, whether you (the Electron team) or the Playwright team implements a solution as long as it is possible at the end to test context menus via Playwright. Maybe, each team has to implement a part of the solution.

### Proposed Solution

An API function  `Menu.getContextMenu()` as a counterpart to `Menu.getApplicationMenu()`.

### Alternatives Considered

Not using an Electron Menu for opening context menus. But:

- It's additional effort to implement and style some menu in HTML/JS/CSS
- It will not be a native menu in the usual operating system style

### Additional Information

I made a while ago a [minimal project](https://github.com/c3er/electron-contextmenu) for showing, what I like to test via Playwright.

nodes.title: Allow passing CLI arguments to autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

It's crucial for apps with background behavior (no window, tray icon only) to update themselves seamlessly without interrupting the user and resume work after update as soon as possible. Nobody likes having their work interrupted when an application they aren't using suddenly restarts and displays its window on top of others. The resulting frustration may be so severe that it even prompt the user to completely abandon the application and uninstall it immediately.

Developers need a way to customize the startup behavior of the updated version. The most common requirement for a seamless background update is to prevent the updated application from spawning a new window if no windows were open before the update. The best way to achieve this is to pass CLI arguments to the updated application and handle them in the new process.

The problem is that `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()` does not provide this capability

### Proposed Solution

Implement the ability to pass CLI arguments to autoUpdater.quitAndInstall() via an optional `Options` object:
```typescript
import { autoUpdater } from 'electron';

autoUpdater.quitAndInstall({
    args: ["--custom-arg-1", "--custom-arg-2", "--custom-arg-3"]
})
```

### Alternatives Considered

1) **Using the `app.relaunch()`**: Ultimately, this method could be used to launch any executable following the main process termination. And it also allows for the passing of CLI arguments. The main disadvantage of this workaround is that it does not respect the new version prepared by the `autoUpdater`, which results in two application instances being launched: the old one and the updated one. You could fix this by manually providing the execPath to the Squirrel.Windows main executable. However, **this isn't a proper solution because app.relaunch() isn't intended for this responsibility**. Communicating with the underlying updating framework is solely the responsibility of the autoUpdater.
2) **Using a temp file**: While transferring data via a temporary file is possible, its main drawback is extremely low performance. This method introduces an additional delay in application window initialization, especially when checking a flag to determine if the window should be created at startup.

### Additional Information

### Electron Version

38.2.1 and many others

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Manjaro, up-to-date (NOT using Wayland)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

Accelerators (shortcuts) should respect my keyboard layout.  That is, the shortcut for "paste" should be `^V`, using my layout's definition of `V` -- I'm using Dvorak, and `V` is where `>`/`.` is located for QWERTY).

### Actual Behavior

Accelerators revert to QWERTY layout - after a while, the shortcut to "paste" becomes `^K` in Dvorak which is the same key as `^V` in QWERTY.  Non-shortcuts, e.g. typing normal text in a Signal message or code in a VSCodium window, correctly uses the global layout; only the accelerators / shortcut keys are wrong.  Non-electron apps are unaffected.

Re-running `setxkbmap -layout us -variant dvorak` fixes it, for a while.  Sometimes days, sometimes hours.  As it is random, I haven't worked out a reliable way to trigger it.  My guess is that it may be related to sleeping or coming back from it?

Note:  I did not "install" QWERTY on this system; it's not in the layout selection menu in xfce4's applet, or in the keyboard layout control panel.  Obviously, it's available to `setxkbmap` if I force it, in a terminal.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/georgedorn/2c155749a84a46de566ae0055ff69e1d

### Additional Information

As I don't have reliable repro steps, I will add more notes when it next happens.  Applications it has affected in the last couple weeks:
- Signal-desktop
- Delta Chat
- VSCodium
- Chromium

It likely affect many other versions; I recall having the issue going back a year, maybe more.

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Chrome 142 is introducing a local network access permissions check and has plans to make it on by default in a future version: [https://developer.chrome.com/blog/local-network-access](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/local-network-access)

This feature is important for security, but having it on could interfere with legitimate use cases site to connect to resources on localhost or a private network.

When testing Electron 39.0.0 beta, this had no effect and I could not get a permissions prompt or query local network access permissions even when adding flags to the command line in Electron.

### Proposed Solution

Include an option for local network access for navigator.permissions.query to allow applications to define their own local network access behavior, and define/document the default behavior for local network access checks.

### Alternatives Considered

Make no changes, but document the default behavior, especially as Chrome/Chromium pushes to make local network access checks always on.

As of testing Electron 39.0.0 beta, local network access checks did not block any localhost communication, so not doing anything is a viable solution.
